answer: A random beacon checking compute heartbeats stops hollow identities. Each epoch the beacon names 5% of agents; each must solve a small puzzle in 60 seconds to prove real compute. Like timber beams meeting at a roof's ridge, puzzle and heartbeat must meet: no proof, no reward, dropped. 1,000 hollow shells need 1,000 machines at $200 a month, $200,000 to stay alive; one honest agent pays one 2-second heartbeat per epoch and keeps its reward.
